Association of Neutrophil-To-Lymphocyte Ratio and Atherogenic Index of Plasma With Angiographically Confirmed Coronary Artery Disease.
items.abstract: BackgroundThe neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) and atherogenic index of plasma (AIP) have been associated with coronary artery disease (CAD). We investigated their associations with angiographically confirmed CAD and lesion severity.MethodsThis retrospective study included 2,933 patients undergoing coronary angiography for suspected CAD at Wuhan Third Hospital. CAD was defined as ≥50% luminal stenosis in at least one major coronary artery or branch. Lesion severity was assessed using the Gensini score. Multivariable logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic analyses were performed.ResultsAmong 2,933 patients, 1,615 had CAD and 1,318 had no significant stenosis. NLR and AIP were higher in patients with CAD and increased across Gensini score categories (all P<0.05). After adjustment, AIP remained independently associated with CAD (OR=1.557, P=0.042), whereas NLR did not (OR=1.019, P=0.581). AIP alone showed limited discrimination (AUC=0.537). A multivariable model including age, blood pressure, fasting blood glucose, and AIP showed an AUC of 0.779. Adding AIP did not significantly improve AUC (DeLong P=0.153) or NRI (0.071, P=0.106), although IDI improvement was significant (0.002, P<0.05).ConclusionsIn patients undergoing coronary angiography for suspected CAD, NLR and AIP were associated with CAD and angiographic disease burden. AIP remained independently associated with CAD, whereas NLR did not. However, AIP showed limited discrimination and no clear incremental improvement beyond conventional variables. These findings do not support population screening or routine clinical implementation.

items.title: High Thrombus Burden in Premature Type 1 Myocardial Infarction: Cross-Sectional Associations With STEMI Presentation, Coronary Flow, and Systemic Inflammation.
items.abstract: We evaluated whether admission complete blood count-derived inflammatory indices were associated with angiographic high thrombus burden (HTB) in premature myocardial infarction (MI). Consecutive patients aged <45 years with type 1 MI and an identifiable culprit lesion who underwent coronary angiography between 2020 and 2024 were included in this single-center, retrospective, cross-sectional analysis. Thrombus burden was assessed using the Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction (TIMI) thrombus grading scale, with occluded vessels reclassified after restoration of coronary flow; HTB was defined as grades 4-5. The neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) and systemic inflammatory response index (SIRI) were evaluated using clinically defined multivariable logistic regression models, with and without adjustment for ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) presentation. Among 137 patients (77 with STEMI and 60 with non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction [NSTEMI]), 81 had an occluded culprit vessel; after restoration of coronary flow, only two lesions remained classified as grade 5. HTB was identified in 79 patients (57.7%) and was associated with STEMI presentation (67.1% vs. 41.4%, P = 0.003) and culprit vessel occlusion (69.6% vs. 44.8%, P = 0.004). Neither NLR (P = 0.54) nor SIRI (P = 0.20) differed significantly between thrombus burden categories, and neither was associated with HTB after adjustment for pre-event characteristics (odds ratio [OR] 1.05, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.94-1.17 and OR 1.13, 95% CI 0.95-1.35, respectively) or additional adjustment for STEMI presentation (OR 1.03, 95% CI 0.92-1.14 and OR 1.08, 95% CI 0.90-1.30, respectively), whereas STEMI presentation remained significantly associated with HTB (OR 2.75, 95% CI 1.33-5.68, P = 0.006). The findings were consistent across all sensitivity analyses, and discriminatory performance was negligible (areas under the curve of 0.531 and 0.564). No significant differences in in-hospital outcomes were detected; however, these comparisons were underpowered. In young patients with angiographically confirmed type 1 MI, HTB was associated with STEMI presentation and initial coronary occlusion but not with admission inflammatory indices.

items.title: Risk Factors, Ischemic Delay, and In-Hospital Outcomes by Sex in Adults Aged 18-50 Years with STEMI Undergoing Primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: An Exploratory Single-Center Cohort.
items.abstract: To describe sex differences in cardiovascular risk factors and reperfusion delays and explore in-hospital outcomes in adults aged 18-50 years with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). This retrospective single-center cohort included 497 consecutive patients (71 [14.3%] women) treated during 2023-2024. Hard major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE) comprised all-cause death, recurrent myocardial infarction, or stroke. A nonstandard expanded clinical deterioration composite additionally included incident cardiogenic shock and, among patients admitted in Killip class I, incident heart failure. Sex comparisons and Firth penalized logistic models were exploratory. Mean age was 40.7 +- 5.3 years. Current smoking was more frequent in men (69.0% vs 39.4%; P < 0.001), whereas obesity was more frequent in women (54.9% vs 26.8%; P < 0.001). Age-adjusted median symptom-to-first-medical-contact, first-medical-contact-to-device, and total ischemic times were 46, 10, and 48 minutes longer in women, respectively (all P < 0.001). Hard MACCE occurred in 21 patients (4.2%), incident heart failure occurred in 13 of 390 eligible patients (3.3%), and the expanded composite occurred in 46 patients (9.3%). The expanded composite occurred in 12 of 71 women and 34 of 426 men (16.9% vs 8.0%; unadjusted P = 0.025), and incident cardiogenic shock occurred in 7 women and 13 men (9.9% vs 3.1%; unadjusted P = 0.015). In the parsimonious baseline model, the adjusted odds ratio (OR) for female sex was 2.61 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.21-5.42), attenuating to 1.90 (95% CI, 0.83-4.18) after adding admission Killip class ≥II. Women had a different risk-factor distribution and longer documented ischemic delays. The association between sex and the expanded composite was sensitive to adjustment for baseline clinical severity. Sex-specific outcome estimates are hypothesis-generating given the small female subgroup and event counts. The retrospective single-center design, absence of post-discharge follow-up, and unavailable care- and referral-pathway variables limit causal interpretation.

items.title: Bee Sting-Associated Kounis Syndrome Presenting as Myocardial Infarction: A Case Report and Systematic Review with Age-Based Analysis.
items.abstract: Kounis syndrome (KS) is an uncommon acute coronary syndrome triggered by allergic or hypersensitivity reactions. Bee stings are a recognized precipitant, although the available evidence is largely limited to case reports and small case series. We present a 44-year-old man with probable bee sting-associated KS and systematically review published cases, including an exploratory age-based comparison using ≤45 years as the cutoff for myocardial infarction in younger individuals. PubMed/Medical Literature Analysis and Retrieval System Online (MEDLINE) and Scopus were searched in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 recommendations. A total of 47 patients were included, comprising 46 previously reported cases and our index case. The mean age was 55.7+-13.0 years, and 39/47 patients (83.0%) were male. Symptoms developed within 30 minutes in 29/47 patients (61.7%), and chest pain occurred in 41/47 (87.2%). Type II KS predominated (29/43, 67.4%), while ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) occurred in 37/47 patients (78.7%), and revascularization was performed in 27/47 (57.4%). Cardiogenic shock, cardiac arrest, and rhythm or conduction disturbances occurred in 11/46 (23.9%), 5/46 (10.9%), and 7/46 patients (15.2%), respectively. Recovery at the last reported assessment was documented in 45/46 patients (97.8%), with no reported deaths. No follow-up data were available after the index patient left the hospital against medical advice approximately five hours after presentation. Thirteen patients (27.7%) were aged ≤45 years; age-stratified descriptive analyses did not reveal clear differences in most clinical characteristics; however, interpretation was limited by the small number of younger patients. Bee sting-associated KS may cause severe acute coronary presentations, including in younger individuals. Given the case-based and heterogeneous nature of the evidence, these findings should be interpreted cautiously and confirmed in systematically collected cohorts.

items.title: TIME to Target Sarcomas: Lessons from the Tumor Immune Microenvironment.
items.abstract: The tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) has emerged as a crucial regulator of antitumor immune responses with important therapeutic, prognostic, and predictive implications. Despite the success of immunotherapies in select solid tumors, notably melanoma and non-small cell lung cancer, their impact in soft-tissue sarcomas (STSs) is limited, often attributed to an immune-cold TIME passively driven by low neoantigen burden. Herein, we review the current understanding of the STS TIME, its variability across STS subtypes, and its implications for STS immunotherapy. We propose that the prevailing view of STSs as passively immune-cold is incomplete and that active tumor-driven immune suppression is likely underappreciated. Distinguishing active from passive immune escape and understanding its mechanistic underpinnings will be important to rationally design effective TIME-targeted therapies in STSs and to serve as a paradigm for therapeutic interventions in other immune-cold tumors.

items.title: Polyclonal breast milk-derived secretory IgA confers broad antiviral protection against multiple respiratory viruses.
items.abstract: Passive immunization is an important tool for protecting individuals with primary immune deficiencies from infectious diseases and offers a rapid response strategy for protecting vulnerable populations, particularly during the interval between pathogen emergence and vaccine deployment. Current approaches rely on intravenous delivery of IgG-enriched plasma or monoclonal antibodies, which limits accessibility, scalability, and effectiveness at mucosal surfaces, the primary entry point for respiratory viruses. Here, we tested LCTG-001, a polyclonal secretory IgA preparation derived from pooled human breast milk, to address these limitations. LCTG-001 demonstrated broad antiviral activity against clinically relevant respiratory viruses, including respiratory syncytial virus, adenovirus, and influenza A virus. LCTG-001 effectively recognized both group 1 and group 2 influenza A subtypes, including the highly pathogenic H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b, and engaged nonneutralizing effector mechanisms such as neuraminidase inhibition and neutrophil activation. When administered intranasally, LCTG-001 conferred complete protection against influenza A challenge in both immunocompetent and antibody-deficient murine models, preventing morbidity and mortality through a transient early reduction in viral burden followed by sustained improvements in lung pathology and lung barrier integrity. These findings highlight the potential of breast milk-derived secretory IgA as a scalable, mucosa-targeted passive immunization strategy capable of addressing both endemic and emerging respiratory viral threats.

items.title: Maternal vaccination with capsular polysaccharide bioconjugates protects against murine Klebsiella pneumoniae neonatal sepsis.
items.abstract: Klebsiella pneumoniae is the leading cause of neonatal sepsis in low- and middle-income countries and the foremost cause of infectious deaths in young children. K. pneumoniae isolates are becoming increasingly resistant to antibiotics, creating a great need for additional therapies or preventative strategies. Maternal vaccination serves as an attractive approach to protect from K. pneumoniae neonatal sepsis. Herein, we report a murine model of maternal immunization followed by pup challenge to evaluate putative K. pneumoniae vaccines. Dams were immunized with capsular polysaccharide bioconjugate vaccines at mating and boosted with two different immunization schedules throughout the gestational period. After parturition, offspring were tested for antigen-specific antibody levels and later challenged with a lethal dose of K. pneumoniae. Pups born to dams immunized with K1- and K2-conjugate vaccines demonstrated significant protection from sepsis relative to control pups. Antibodies transferred from vaccinated dams persisted and remained protective in pups for at least six weeks after birth. Collectively these results demonstrate a feasible and reproducible murine model of maternal immunization verifying the efficacy of bioconjugate vaccines in protecting against lethal neonatal K. pneumoniae infection.

items.title: Macrophage- or neutrophil-expressed UPP1 drives tumor growth and immune suppression in the tumor microenvironment.
items.abstract: Uridine phosphorylase 1 (UPP1) has recently emerged as a metabolic regulator with critical roles in tumor cell biology. However, its expression pattern and functional significance in nonmalignant components of the tumor microenvironment (TME) remain largely unexplored. Here, we performed a comprehensive pan-cancer single-cell transcriptomic analysis revealing that UPP1 is highly expressed not only in tumor cells but also in tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) and neutrophils (TANs). Clinically, UPP1 expression in TAMs and TANs correlates with poor prognosis and diminished response to immunotherapy across multiple cancer types. Mechanistically, UPP1 up-regulation could be driven by NF-κB signaling. Functionally, UPP1 reprograms macrophages toward a tumor-promoting phenotype, characterized by enhanced glycolysis, ATP-adenosine signaling activation, and increased production of immunosuppressive cytokines such as granulocyte colony-stimulating factor. In neutrophils, UPP1 also supports TAN polarization, influences neutrophil extracellular trap release, and contributes to broad immunosuppressive remodeling. In vivo, targeting UPP1 in macrophages or neutrophils reprograms the immune landscape and restrains tumor progression. Together, our findings uncover a previously underappreciated role of UPP1 in nonmalignant immune populations and establish it as a key immune mediator within the TME, offering a potentially promising therapeutic target for enhancing antitumor immunity.

items.title: Immune biomarkers of response and resistance to ipilimumab and nivolumab in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer.
items.abstract: Immune checkpoint therapies have shown limited efficacy in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC). The AMADEUS prostate expansion cohort (NCT03651271) evaluated the efficacy, safety, and biomarkers of escalating ipilimumab doses combined with nivolumab. Patients received ipilimumab 1 milligram per kilogram (mg/kg) + nivolumab 360 mg (I1+N360), ipilimumab 3 mg/kg + nivolumab 1 mg/kg (I3+N1), or ipilimumab 5 mg/kg + nivolumab 1 mg/kg (I5+N1). Coprimary endpoints were 6-month disease control rate (DCR) and changes in tumoral CD8 percentage. Thirty-two patients were enrolled. DCRs were 33% (4 of 12) for I1+N360, 20% (1 of 5) for I3+N1, and 20% (3 of 15) for I5+N1. Across cohorts, tumoral CD8 percentage increased by a median of 5.0%. Although higher ipilimumab doses were tolerable, I1+N360 achieved similar disease control and immune activation with a more favorable safety profile. Early disease progression was associated with increased expression of a TREM2-associated myeloid gene signature, which was also significantly enriched in two independent prostate cancer datasets.

items.title: Acute Alcohol-Associated Hepatitis: The Role of Liver Transplantation.
items.abstract: Severe alcohol-associated hepatitis (AH) remains one of the most challenging syndromes in hepatology and critical care, with high short-term mortality despite advances in supportive management. Although corticosteroids remain the only guideline-endorsed pharmacologic therapy shown to improve early survival, their benefit is modest, limited to selected patients, and frequently complicated by infection. Consequently, contemporary management extends well beyond corticosteroid therapy and requires meticulous supportive care, nutritional optimization, infection surveillance, management of portal hypertensive complications and acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF), and early multidisciplinary involvement. This review summarizes the current evidence regarding the diagnosis, prognostic assessment, and medical management of severe AH. Key prognostic models, including MELD, Maddrey Discriminant Function, and the Lille score, are discussed together with evolving evidence supporting individualized corticosteroid use and emerging investigational therapies. Particular emphasis is placed on critically ill patients with ACLF, in whom extrahepatic organ failure often supersedes liver dysfunction as the principal determinant of outcome. The review also examines the evolving role of early liver transplantation (LT), one of the most important paradigm shifts in modern transplant hepatology. Contemporary approaches to patient selection, psychosocial assessment, relapse-risk evaluation, living donor transplantation, and the management of patients with catastrophic AH are discussed, along with ethical considerations surrounding organ allocation, medical urgency, and stewardship of scarce donor organs. Despite important advances in supportive care and transplantation, severe AH continues to carry substantial mortality. Optimizing outcomes requires timely diagnosis, multidisciplinary management, careful selection for medical therapy, and early recognition of patients unlikely to recover without liver transplantation.

items.title: A comprehensive evaluation on the impact of MASLD on the prognosis of chronic hepatitis B-related hepatocellular carcinoma following hepatectomy: results from retrospective multicenter cohort study and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Prognosis after radical hepatectomy for chronic hepatitis B (CHB) related hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is poor. Comorbidity of CHB and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) has grown increasingly common, with MASLD further modifying the hepatic microenvironment beyond HBV-induced injury. However, its impact on postoperative prognosis remains unclear. Combining a retrospective study with meta-analysis, this study systematically compared prognostic differences and influencing factors in 424 hepatectomy patients (MASLD-CHB-HCC group vs. CHB-HCC group) from multiple centers. Additionally, a meta-analysis involving 6653 patients was performed to further verify the prognostic effect of MASLD. In this retrospective cohort study, the MASLD-CHB-HCC group showed significantly superior overall survival (OS) (p = 0.041) and recurrence-free survival (RFS) (p = 0.028) compared with the CHB-HCC group, with statistically significant differences. However, after performing propensity score matching (PSM) screening, no statistical differences were observed in OS (p = 0.220) and RFS (p = 0.190) between the two groups. This result is consistent with our meta-analysis conclusion. Cox regression analysis demonstrated that higher body mass index (BMI) was an independent factor associated with favorable survival. In subgroup analyses stratified by different BMI cutoffs, among non-lean patients, the MASLD-CHB-HCC group achieved better OS (BMI ≥ 23 subgroup: p < 0.001; BMI ≥ 25 subgroup: p < 0.001) and RFS (BMI ≥ 23 subgroup: p < 0.001; BMI ≥ 25 subgroup: p < 0.001). MASLD exerts differential impacts on survival prognosis in patients with CHB-HCC, with divergent effects observed between lean and non-lean subgroups stratified by BMI.

items.title: Infectious necrotic hepatitis caused by Clostridium novyi type B in a goat with listeriosis.
items.abstract: A 6-y-old postpartum Nubian crossbreed goat was submitted for postmortem examination following a clinical course of ataxia, lateral head tilt, and recumbency. The liver had a poorly defined, pale-yellow focally extensive lesion and focal thickening of bile ducts. Histologically, an area of extensive coagulative necrosis was surrounded by many viable and degranulated neutrophils and gram-positive bacilli, which were identified as Clostridium novyi by immunohistochemistry. Numerous neutrophilic infiltrates were observed in the brainstem. PCR on DNA extracted from hepatic tissue was positive for the fliC , tcna , and tcnb genes of C. novyi type B. Additionally, PCR testing of brainstem tissue was positive for the hlyA gene of Listeria monocytogenes . To our knowledge, infectious necrotic hepatitis (INH), confirmed by molecular testing and with concurrent listeriosis, has not been reported previously in a goat. Clostridial hepatitis in animals is typically triggered by anaerobic conditions within the liver parenchyma, which facilitate the germination of dormant spores and the subsequent release of potent toxins. Although flukes were not observed, the presumptive inciting hypoxic event leading to parenchymal necrosis in this case was Fasciola hepatica larval migration. Because the clinical and pathology features of INH caused by C. novyi type B and bacillary hemoglobinuria caused by C. haemolyticum are nearly identical, molecular differentiation is essential to establish an accurate etiologic diagnosis.

items.title: Evaluating hepatitis C viremia and antiviral treatment barriers in hemodialysis patients in the post-HCV elimination era: Experience from Ain Shams University Hospitals.
items.abstract: Egypt historically maintained a high prevalence of hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection, with maintenance hemodialysis (HD) patients facing increased risk due to frequent invasive procedures. Following the 2014 launch of Egypt's National HCV Elimination initiative, overall population prevalence declined substantially. However, contemporary data evaluating active viremia and treatment barriers among prevalent HD patients remain limited. To assess the seroprevalence (anti-HCV antibodies) and active viremia (HCV RNA by PCR) among prevalent HD patients after implementation of the National Eradication Initiative, and to identify the barriers to antiviral treatment despite free therapy. A multicenter cross-sectional study was conducted between November 2023 and April 2024 across three affiliated hemodialysis units at Ain Shams University Hospitals, Cairo, Egypt. A total of 410 adult patients (aged ≥ 18 years) on regular maintenance HD for >6 months were recruited using consecutive sampling. Anti HCV antibodies were determined using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), and active infection was confirmed via quantitative real-time HCV RNA PCR testing. Sociodemographic features, dialysis vintage, treatment history, and self-reported reasons for non-treatment were evaluated. The mean age of participants was 47.1 ± 18.2 years, with a male predominance (62.4%, n= 256). Anti-HCV antibody positivity was identified in 113 of 410 patients (27.6%). Among anti-HCV-positive patients, active viremia (HCV PCR positive) was confirmed in only 14/113 cases (12.4% of seropositive patients; overall study population prevalence of active viremia: 14/410; 3.4%). Of the 113 anti-HCV-positive patients, 95/113 (84.1%) had received antiviral therapy, with 93/95 (97.8%) achieving viral clearance (sustained virological response, SVR). Un-treated patients were (15.9%, n=18). Treatment barriers included lack of awareness regarding free treatment availability (27.8%), fear of side effects (22.2%), treatment refusal (11.1%), and incomplete paperwork (11.1%). HCV PCR positivity was significantly associated with a lack of prior DAA treatment (85.7% vs 6.1%}, p < 0.001) and longer dialysis vintage (5.08 ± 1.1 vs 2.96 ± 1.13 years, p=0.018). In conclusion, the relatively reduced prevalence of HCV in this study reflects the success of the national eradication initiative. Nevertheless, gaps remain in awareness and accessibility, which may hinder complete eradication in high-risk groups such as hemodialysis patients. Enhanced patient education, strict infection-control measures and targeted patient support is crucial to address residual gaps in high-risk dialysis units.

items.title: The Association between Vitiligo and Infections: A Systematic Review.
items.abstract: Vitiligo is an acquired depigmentation disease with an unknown etiology. Several theories on its etiology have been proposed, including autoimmune mechanisms, oxidative stress, genetic factors, environmental factors, and lack of melanocyte growth factor. Recent studies have demonstrated a possible correlation between microbial infections and the development or consequences of vitiligo. This study aims to investigate the potential association between microbial infections and vitiligo, focusing on identifying any explainable correlations between these two. A systematic search was performed on all publications evaluating the effects of viral, bacterial, parasitic, and fungal infections on vitiligo using online databases such as PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science from 2010 up to June 2023 and followed the preferred reporting items for systematic review and meta-analysis (PRISMA) checklist. Viral infections, such as human immunodeficiency virus, varicella-zoster, and hepatitis C, are suggested triggers of vitiligo, potentially through immune dysregulation, cytokine imbalances, the Koebner phenomenon, and altered cellular immunity. Activation of MDA5 and vitamin D deficiency have also been proposed as mechanisms for virus-induced vitiligo. Infection with severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) can dysregulate CD8+ lymphocytes and activate proinflammatory cytokines, disrupting immune tolerance and triggering or exacerbating vitiligo. Additionally, bystander activation triggered by coronavirus may cause an immune response against the host's melanocytes. Other factors such as Helicobacter pylori infection, endophytic bacterial and fungal infections, and vitamin D deficiency may also contribute to vitiligo pathogenesis by altering cellular immunity and systemic inflammation. Overall, a better understanding of the multiple factors that contribute to vitiligo may help inform more effective treatments and management strategies for this challenging condition.

items.title: The neogenin-hemojuvelin axis in murine liver is crucial for hepcidin expression.
items.abstract: Neogenin (NEO1) is a ubiquitously expressed, multifunctional receptor that binds hemojuvelin (HJV); both proteins are essential components within hepatocytes for maintaining systemic iron homeostasis. Previous research established that the targeted ablation of hepatic Neo1 or Hjv in mice markedly reduces expression of the central iron-regulatory hormone, hepcidin. Reduction in hepcidin results in unrestricted iron absorption that leads to severe systemic iron overload. Hepatic hepcidin expression is primarily induced via the bone morphogenetic protein (BMP) signaling pathway, which requires a complex of plasma membrane proteins, including HJV acting as a BMP coreceptor. However, the precise mechanism by which NEO1 and HJV are orchestrated to robustly activate this pathway remains poorly understood. In this study, we systemically investigated the mechanisms by which hepatic Neo1 coordinates with Hjv to facilitate hepcidin induction using various knockout mouse models. Our data indicate that although Hjv is a more potent inducer of hepcidin than hepatic Neo1, the simultaneous ablation of both Neo1 and Hjv greatly reduces hepcidin expression. These results suggest that these two proteins form a crucial functional axis for controlling hepcidin levels. Further analysis revealed that ∼84% of hepcidin expression relies on the synergistic association of Neo1 with Hjv. In comparison, Hjv retains a significantly compromised (∼12%) ability to induce hepcidin independently of Neo1, whereas Neo1 possesses only a residual (∼3%) independent induction capacity. Collectively, these data support a model in which hepatic Neo1 acts primarily as a molecular scaffold to facilitate assembly of the hepcidin-inducing signaling complex through Hjv. NEW & NOTEWORTHY Hepcidin expression in hepatocytes relies on a multiprotein plasma membrane complex. This study establishes a critical functional axis between neogenin and hemojuvelin within this complex, revealing how their coordination is essential for systemic iron homeostasis. Our findings provide a new mechanistic framework for understanding the assembly of the hepcidin-signaling complex.

items.title: Metabolomic aging and mortality clocks based on ensemble learning identify systemic aging risk across the human life span in 18,476 individuals.
items.abstract: Aging is characterized by progressive functional decline, yet metabolomic signatures across the human life span remain incompletely defined. Here, we profiled plasma metabolomes from 18,476 participants aged 1 to 96 years across six centers in China using nano-assisted laser desorption/ionization mass spectrometry (LDI-MS) and identified 56 representative age-associated metabolites. In a healthy cohort, we developed a stacking ensemble model to estimate metabolomic age and quantified metabolomic age acceleration (mAA) as each individual's deviation from chronological age. Higher mAA was associated with health deterioration and unfavorable lifestyles. During follow-up from 2019 to 2025, individuals with accelerated mAA showed increased risk of incident chronic diseases, such as fatty liver disease, hypertension, and diabetes, as well as increased all-cause mortality. In a disease cohort, we further developed a mortality-linked metabolomic metric (age deviation) that quantified individualized departures from age-expected mortality risk inferred from plasma metabolites. Age deviation was associated with established composite health measures and increased with multisystem disease involvement and higher multimorbidity burden. Together, these findings support the potential of plasma metabolomic profiling as a scalable, life span-wide approach for deriving clinically interpretable metabolomic aging metrics associated with health status, chronic disease risk, and mortality.

items.title: Bile, sulphur and carbohydrate metabolic variation co-occur with host adiposity in mice colonized with primate microbiota.
items.abstract: Although mechanistic links between the microbiome and chronic disease are increasingly well defined, how microbiomes facilitate normal variation in host metabolism remains less clear. Building on our recent demonstration that pooled faecal inocula from different primate species can cause relative differences in mouse host adiposity, we define potential mechanisms by which this could occur. Using existing samples from germ-free mice inoculated with faecal samples from humans ( Homo sapiens ), rhesus macaques ( Macaca mulatta ) and squirrel monkeys ( Saimiri boliviensis ), we integrate shotgun metagenomics of caecal contents, liquid chromatography-MS-MS metabolomics of serum and caecal contents and hepatic RNA-sequencing. Our multi-omic analysis reveals that the relative increase in adiposity previously observed in macaque-donor mice is associated with differences in hepatic cysteine catabolism and bile metabolism pathway features. These data suggest that bile and sulphur co-metabolic variation may mediate increased bile pool hydrophobicity. We also observed variation in caecal microbiome composition as well as host hepatic retinol signalling and lipid metabolism between treatments. When considered together with the observation that macaque-donor mice consumed less food than the other treatment groups, our results support the hypothesis that increased bile pool hydrophobicity results in increased dietary energy extraction. Our findings provide a foundation for future mechanistic testing of new hypotheses for understanding how the intestinal microbiomes of different primate species regulate lipid homeostasis in a mouse host.

items.title: Bariatric Surgery and Risk of Obesity-Related Cancer by Age and Sex.
items.abstract: Obesity is associated with elevated risks for multiple cancers. How bariatric surgery influences these risks across age and sex is insufficiently understood. To evaluate the association between bariatric surgery and obesity-related cancer (breast, endometrial, ovarian, esophageal adenocarcinoma, liver, pancreatic, colon, rectal, kidney, and multiple myeloma) and whether this association varies by age and sex. This population-based cohort study within the Nordic Obesity Surgery Cohort (NordOSCo) included individuals aged 18 to 59 years with an obesity record in Denmark, Finland, or Sweden from 1992 to 2023. Prospectively collected data on exposure, outcomes, and confounders were obtained from well-maintained national registries. Follow-up continued until cancer diagnosis, death, emigration, or December 31, 2023. These data were analyzed from December 2025 to April 2026. Bariatric surgery vs no surgery among individuals with obesity. The primary outcome was incidence of obesity-related cancers. Risks were compared using crude and multivariable-adjusted incidence rate ratios (aIRR) with 95% CIs derived from Poisson regression adjusted for age, sex, calendar year, country, and obesity- and lifestyle-related comorbidities. Effect modification by age group (18-39 vs 40-59 years) and sex (female vs male) was evaluated using interaction terms. Among 784 105 individuals with obesity (569 266 women [73%] and 214 839 men [27%]), 99 614 underwent bariatric surgery. Surgery was associated with a lower risk of obesity-related cancer overall (aIRR, 0.81; 95% CI, 0.77-0.85). The magnitude of risk reduction did not differ by age group (individuals aged 18 to 39 years: aIRR, 0.80; 95% CI, 0.72-0.88 and individuals aged 40 to 59 years: aIRR, 0.81; 95% CI, 0.78-0.86) (P for interaction = .88). Associations for non-sex-specific cancers were similar in men and women (P for interaction = .50). For individual cancers, the strongest inverse associations were observed for liver cancer (aIRR, 0.49; 95% CI, 0.34-0.70), endometrial cancer (aIRR, 0.51; 95% CI, 0.45-0.59), and ovarian cancer (aIRR, 0.73; 95% CI, 0.60-0.87). In contrast, pancreatic cancer risk was increased after surgery, particularly among younger adults (aIRR, 2.21; 95% CI, 1.44-3.39; P = .01). In this study, bariatric surgery was associated with a lower long-term risk of obesity-related cancers, with similar associations across age groups and sexes. These findings suggest that the long-term oncologic benefits of bariatric surgery apply broadly across age groups and sexes, supporting equitable access to bariatric surgery for patients with obesity.

items.title: Alistipes-derived monomethyl branched-chain fatty acid iso-15:0 suppresses hepatocellular carcinoma progression by inhibiting Gβγ/PI3K/AKT signaling.
items.abstract: The role of gut microbiota and their metabolites in the progression of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) has garnered increasing attention. Although Alistipes, a genus frequently reported as a beneficial bacterium, has been associated with antitumor effects and enhanced efficacy of cancer therapies, its specific functions and underlying mechanisms in HCC remain poorly defined. In this study, 16S rDNA sequencing revealed a marked decrease in the abundance of Alistipes in fecal samples from HCC patients compared to healthy controls, a finding that was also observed in HCC mouse models. Additionally, iso-15:0, an important fatty acid metabolite derived from Alistipes, was found to be significantly reduced in the feces of both HCC patients and HCC mouse models. Functional experiments demonstrated that iso-15:0 effectively suppresses the proliferation and migration of HCC cells in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistically, iso-15:0 inhibits the activation of the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway by interfering with G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) downstream signaling, specifically through the Gβγ subunits. To further explore the potential for the clinical application of iso-15:0, we have developed a biomimetic nanodelivery system (3R/RGD/M1@iso-15:0 LNP) that markedly improves the delivery efficiency and therapeutic efficacy of iso-15:0 in vivo. Our findings elucidate for the first time that iso-15:0, derived from Alistipes, suppresses HCC progression by restricting the Gβγ-PI3K/AKT signaling axis, highlighting its potential as a novel therapeutic strategy for HCC.
